summary: Bly, Klamath County: a Forest Service tower (1958) at the Bly Ranger Station was dismantled in 2007; its 7x7 cab stood in the community park as of a 2022 visit.

facts.design: 20-foot treated-timber tower with a 7x7 flat-roof cab and catwalk; only the cab survives
facts.status_note: The 20-foot tower was dismantled in 2007; only its cab survives, displayed in Bly's community park as of a 2022 visit.

staffing.status: used only during emergencies (2022 blog); under emergency status per 1959 inspection

access.note: As of a June 2022 blog visit, the cab stood in a small community park in Bly, less than a mile from the Ranger Station. The blog does not say whether visitors may go inside the cab.

events.note: First lookout at the Bly station: a platform on a warehouse roof at the Klamath FPA station (predates the tower)
20-foot timber tower with 7x7 flat-roof cab built in the Bly Ranger Station compound. The register's Built field says 1950
Regional Office of Engineering inspection (September 9 visit); the lookout was under emergency status
Decommissioned and scheduled to move to a local park as an interpretive center; the move was delayed a year for lack of a way to move the building
Tower and cab dismantled; the superstructure was destroyed
Cab moved to the community park in Bly

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's Built field says 1950, but the register's own description, the Weebly page and the blog all give 1958 for the tower. FFLOS places the tower after the KFPA station closed in the mid-1950s. The story follows 1958.

notes_for_editor: This is the cab of the Bly Ranger Station tower, so it overlaps us-or-bly-ranger (story written) and us-or-bly-ranger-at-bly-city-park (research only). A human should merge or retire the duplicates. The record's coordinates (42.39799, -121.04287) sit about 90 m from the register's coordinates for the original tower (N 42.398470 W 121.043370), so they mark the Ranger Station, not the park. The sources give no park coordinates. Build year is disputed (register Built field 1950 vs its own description 1958); 1958 is followed. The 2022 blog is a single personal visit report.
